main_result.name: QFORM-CROSS-FRESNEL-DIMENSION-TRADE-v1
main_result.statement_short: For a genuine rank-k source-bank crossing and an ell-rank same-side Fresnel block retained on the original product receiver bank, augmented-row leverage <=1/2 yields |phi(t)| <= M_I 2^(k+ell) pi^(k+ell/2) [|det Gamma| det G]^-1/2 |t|^-(k+ell/2), hence a continuous bounded density whenever k+ell/2>1.
main_result.new_dual_branch: k=1, ell=2 gives <=2^(11/4)[|det Gamma|det G]^-1/4 using M_I<=sqrt(2)

target_application: Diffuse two-bank Walsh family with one crossing direction and two orthogonal receiver curvature directions has spectrum {1,-1,1,1}, G=I_3, and density <=2^(11/4)=6.7271713220... for every independent cap-one input law.
partner_application: account02/B16 r35 applied to Q+theta(c1^T X_I)^2: carrier eigenvalues ((theta+-sqrt(theta^2+4))/2,1,-1,1), at least four have modulus >=1 counting one from the first pair, and density <=(5/3)2^(8/5)=5.0523885550... for every real theta. Its source-innovation threshold s1*s2*delta>=2^-10 gives density <80.839.
corrections_preserved: A bounded joint projection density alone does not control an arbitrary indefinite curved trace.
Small source innovations cannot be deleted on unbounded inputs.

Two independent arbitrary bounded-density 3D bank laws can still retain the dependent twisted-Wiener obstruction after convolution; the new theorem avoids this by keeping the receiver bank factorized in original scalar sources.
next_implication: QFORM-TWO-BANK-CURVATURE-DIMENSION-EXTRACTION-v1: force the ultra-coloop two-bank survivor into a source decomposition with k+ell/2>1, row leverages <=1/2 and |det Gamma|det G bounded below, or construct a source-preserving joint receiver for the residual fully degenerate augmented-innovation case.
